verdict.oneLiner: Notion OAuth is supported via Composio, requires no special gates, and can be used for sign‑in, read, or write access.

steps.title: Set up Notion account and workspace admin rights
steps.detail: Log into Notion, ensure you are an admin of a workspace where the integration will be installed. This is required to create a public connection in the Notion developer portal.

steps.title: Create a new public connection in Notion developer portal
steps.detail: Navigate to Notion’s developer portal, click “New public connection”, and fill out the form. Provide a name, description, and select required scopes (e.g., read, read:database).

steps.title: Add Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: In the Notion connection form, set the Redirect URI exactly to the value shown in Composio’s Notion Toolkit dashboard (decoded value of `redirect_uri`). The URI must match byte‑for‑byte.

blockers.workaround: Copy the URI from Composio dashboard, decode it if necessary, and paste it verbatim.

steps.title: Enable Managed Auth in Composio
steps.detail: In Composio, add a new Notion connection using the Toolkit. Choose “Managed Auth” so Composio handles the OAuth flow for end‑users. The dashboard will display the callback URL; confirm it matches the Notion redirect URI set earlier.

steps.title: Validate OAuth flow with a test user
steps.detail: Use a separate Notion account (not the admin) to trigger the authorization flow via Composio’s demo link. Verify you receive an access token and can call read endpoints within the 180 req/min limit.

blockers.text: Refresh token invalidation after scope change
blockers.workaround: Avoid changing scopes after initial test; if you must, re‑authorize the test user.

steps.title: Submit integration for production
steps.detail: In Notion’s portal, mark the connection as public, accept terms, provide legal info, and submit. No extra business or security verification is required per settled gates.

steps.title: Await Notion review
steps.detail: Notion will review the public connection; no additional steps required while waiting.

steps.title: Go live – enable for all users
steps.detail: After approval, set the connection status to “Live” in Notion and ensure Composio’s managed auth is enabled for external users. Monitor usage to stay within rate limits.

whileYouWait.text: Continue using Composio’s managed auth for internal testing and prototype features.
Create documentation and demo scripts for end‑users to reduce churn caused by OAuth complexity.

gotchas.text: Redirect URI must match exactly; any encoding differences cause rejection.
Refresh tokens can be invalidated if scopes or config change after initial auth.
Notion’s rate limits (≈180 req/min) may throttle high‑volume production usage.
